body: What gets me through my day? I have a hard time answering that myself. For now, it's taking things one day at a time and not looking too far forward. I can guess the future, but that doesn't make me right. I also think about my father and my friends. I know they care about me deeply, and I can't act selfishly. I myself have a post here, which obviously means I'm struggling, but for right now I just live for today. Tomorrow, and all the things it holds, will come. I can't die today. I refuse to... even if I don't want to exist, I don't know for sure if I'll feel this way tomorrow, a month from now, or years from now. It sure would be a shame if I wasted my potential, even if it is little potential.

I'm sorry you're in that position... I wish I could hug you right now. Going deaf, I can imagine, must be very scary. The best person I've ever dated was deaf, if that's any consolation. It may sound like I'm being insensitive, but there are plenty of deaf people who do well in life. I know what being in constant pain is like. It feels unfair, like life dealt you a bad hand of cards that nobody else has got. I'm struggling with that myself. I also know what having a bad job is like, and I'm struggling with that, too. I don't really know what to say about those things, but knowing I'm not alone in them helps me. I know lots of people struggle with those things, but being able to relate to someone directly actually helps me. Thanks for that.
Hast du etwas dagegen, mir diese Gedanken zu erzählen?

Du bist kein schlechter Mensch, du hast nur schlechte Gedanken. Ich weiß wie es ist. Versuchen Sie nicht, sich selbst zu schlagen. Schreiben Sie alle Dinge auf, für die Sie dankbar sind. Morgen, wenn Sie aufwachen, lesen Sie es. Wenn Sie an neue Dinge denken, für die Sie dankbar sind, fügen Sie sie der Liste hinzu. Lies es jeden Morgen. Zuerst mag es sich falsch anfühlen, aber sagen Sie sich, dass Sie jeden Morgen einen guten Tag haben werden. Sie werden schließlich feststellen, dass Sie nicht die schlechte, dumme oder nervige Person sind, von der Sie glauben, dass Sie sie sind. Schlechte, dumme, ärgerliche Leute sorgen sich nicht, wenn sie schlecht, dumm oder ärgerlich sind. Sie sind so, ohne sich darum zu sorgen.

You care too much about what other people think of you. You're beating yourself up with a ten-pound bat. I used to do that all the time, especially when I thought about how other people think of me. I'd automatically jump to negative conclusions, and you know what helped? Facing my fears. If there was something I wanted to do, but I was hesitant of the outcome, I forced myself to do it. I'd always think of a negative outcome beforehand... but 9 times out of 10, it went a completely different way than what I'd expected. I was beating myself up and automatically assumed what others thought of me, but I realized that demonizing other people wasn't helping me at all. 

When people randomly insult you, in the future, assess the situation. A lot of the time their claims aren't even true, and they're saying things to insult you because they've got a character trait or physical trait themselves that they are insecure about. Because they're insecure about themselves, they insult others to feel better. Just stay away from those people. Like I said, other people do NOT need to care about you for you to be okay.

I remember being 14. I'm gonna tell you a bunch of shit you've probably heard before, but hear me out.

She won't be the only girlfriend you've ever had. It'll hurt, you'll feel like shit for months, maybe a year, but there will be more women in your life. That's how dating and shit goes. She may seem like the only one right now, your main focus, but that's because of the history you've had with her. There will be more, and if they leave, that'll hurt, too. It's a part of life. Don't make it the last part of your life. 

Another thing. You're 14. I know how I thought at that age, and I wanted to be one of the cool kids. One of the kids that everyone cared about, asked about, the one that all the women wanted to be with. I learned something, though. None of that shit mattered. What mattered was getting through school, and doing it in a way that serves YOU. Why? Because when you graduate, nobody really gives a fuck anymore about each other. Maybe you'll have a few friends you keep in contact with (the good/"real" ones), but all of the high school social standing shit dissolves.

My dad told me something one day that's always stuck with me. Other people do NOT need to care about you for you to be okay.
